bulletins.title: Fake Google Reviews Used to Extort Business Owners
bulletins.summary: Scammers post fake negative Google Business reviews (sometimes with hate comments or inappropriate images), then message the owner as "digital marketers" demanding payment to remove those reviews and claimed "hidden reviews," threatening to publish them unless paid quickly. Do not pay — report reviews/profiles as fake in the official Google tools and document everything.

bulletins.title: Fake Purchase Alerts Push Victims to Call Scammer Callback Numbers
bulletins.summary: Scammers send SMS, email, app notifications, or calendar invites claiming an unrecognized purchase ($300–$2000) from brands like PayPal, Norton, McAfee, Microsoft, Shop, or Apple. The message includes a phone number to 'cancel' the charge. Calling connects to fraudsters who harvest card details, push remote-access software, demand gift cards, or request money 'sent back'.
phrases: never call the number in the message

bulletins.title: Fake Amazon/YouTube Recruiter SMS Moves Victims to WhatsApp Task Top-Ups
bulletins.summary: Unsolicited SMS impersonates recruiters for Amazon, YouTube, or similar brands offering high-pay remote 'e-commerce assistant' or listing-optimization tasks. Victims are moved to WhatsApp, complete tasks, may receive a small payout, then must 'top up' crypto or deposit their own money to unlock earnings — which is never returned. University job boards are also being targeted.
phrases: never pay money to start a job

bulletins.title: Government and Boss Impersonators Demand Gift-Card Payments
bulletins.summary: FTC-highlighted imposter scripts: callers or texters claim to be the government (including the FTC), your boss, or another authority and demand urgent payment via gift cards / 'Google certificates'. Real agencies and employers never ask for gift-card numbers or PINs.
phrases: pay the fine with gift cards
only scammers ask for gift cards

bulletins.title: Unexpected Package Delivery Texts With Malicious Links
bulletins.summary: FTC warns that unexpected package-delivery messages with links are often phishing to steal personal and financial information. Carriers and stores should be checked only via the official app or a URL you type yourself.

bulletins.title: Fake GOV.IL Payment SMS Injected Into Legitimate Government Threads
bulletins.summary: Israel National Cyber Directorate warns of phishing SMS that request payment and include a malicious link, appearing inside existing legitimate GOV.IL message threads on some devices. Not a breach of GOV.IL systems — an SMS display trick. Never tap the link or enter card details; pay only via the official site/app you open yourself. Report to 119.

bulletins.title: myGov and ATO Phishing Links During Tax-Time Rush
bulletins.summary: Victoria Police warns scammers SMS/email fake myGov and ATO links to steal sign-in details, redirect tax refunds, or create fraudulent payments. ATO and myGov never send SMS/email links to access services — type my.gov.au or ato.gov.au yourself. Also watch fake retailer stores during end-of-financial-year sales.

bulletins.title: Bank Impersonators Harvest SMS OTP Codes on Cold Calls
bulletins.summary: A private-number caller claims to be the victim's bank, recites a known ID number, says someone is breaking into the account right now, then asks the victim to read back an SMS one-time code. The OTP SMS may even appear in the existing bank message thread, which increases trust.
phrases: i am calling from your bank
someone is trying to break into your account
tell me the code from the sms
i will send you a code by text
one time code to secure your account

bulletins.title: Fan DMs Ask for Birthday Wish Videos to Deepfake Bank KYC
bulletins.summary: Scammers DM creators and everyday users on Instagram or Facebook posing as fans, then ask for a short birthday greeting video. With AI they remix the selfie-style clip into a synthetic KYC/liveness video used to open bank accounts, take loans, or access government systems in the victim's name.
phrases: i am a fan of your content

bulletins.title: Phishing Debt Links Injected Into Legitimate App SMS Threads
bulletins.summary: Attackers inject fake 'settle your debt' texts into existing SMS conversation threads with trusted brands (parking apps like Pango, coffee chains like Cofix) and even government notification threads (Gov.il). Because the lure sits under prior legitimate receipts, victims tap the link and enter card details on a clone site.

bulletins.title: AI Voice-Clone Family Emergency Calls — Use a Shared Code Word
bulletins.summary: Scammers clone a relative's voice with AI and place an urgent 'emergency' call asking for money. Families should agree on a shared emergency code word before wiring anything. One case cited ~450,000 ILS lost.
phrases: do not send money without the code

bulletins.title: Cold-Calling Fraudsters Target Seniors with Gold Bar Courier Scheme
bulletins.summary: Impersonators calling victims claim their financial accounts are at immediate risk and instruct them to remain on the phone while liquidating savings to buy gold bars. Scammers then dispatch a physical courier to the victim's home under the guise of transferring the gold to a safe vault.
phrases: your money is at immediate risk

bulletins.title: Fraudsters Impersonate FBI and IC3 Agents in Asset Recovery Scams
bulletins.summary: Scammers are contacting previous cybercrime victims via direct messages, posing as FBI or IC3 representatives. They claim to offer professional scam recovery services to trace transactions and retrieve lost funds, ultimately attempting to solicit money or personal credentials.

bulletins.title: Romance Scammers Leverage Fake Travel Crises for Wire Demands
bulletins.summary: Online romance scammers groom victims over messaging platforms like WhatsApp without speaking in person, then fabricate sudden emergencies to request urgent wire transfers. Script tactics involve claiming to be stranded, unable to buy plane tickets, or in immediate danger.
phrases: could not get a plane ticket
